checks.explanation: No ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine was reached within 2-3 weeks of this recording; the war continued for years.
The active fighting phase of the Russia-Ukraine war was not nearly over in April 2022; it continued for years afterward.
No globally declared widespread famine occurred by the end of 2022, partly due to the Black Sea Grain Initiative easing Ukrainian grain exports.
No humanitarian disaster of hundreds of millions starving occurred within a year, though food insecurity did worsen in several vulnerable regions.

The US economy did face significant inflation and slowdown pressures through 2022, but attributing this primarily and specifically to severing Russia from the global economy versus broader multifactorial causes is difficult to isolate.
A Chinese invasion of Taiwan has not been taken off the table; tensions and Chinese military activity around Taiwan actually escalated significantly in subsequent years through 2022-2025.
No official 2022 US recession occurred, and national average gas prices peaked around $5 per gallon in June 2022, well short of the predicted $7-10 range.
Equity markets remained volatile and declined through spring 2022 amid rising rate-hike fears rather than sustaining a melt-up.
Inflation was not tamed in the second half of 2022, peaking at 9.1% in June, and the Fed raised rates well above 2.5% (to 4.25-4.5% by year end) rather than sustaining that lower range.
Financial markets remained volatile and generally declined rather than showing constructive dynamics through the predicted window into May 2022.
The stock market's near-term direction from March 2022 was choppy and ultimately downward through the rest of the year rather than steadily upward.
Private-market startup valuations and revenue multiples did continue compressing toward pre-COVID norms through 2022-2023 in a sustained repricing.
The 2022 market downturn proved to be a prolonged bear market rather than a quick rebound within a few weeks.

No formal Russia-Ukraine peace deal was signed in 2022, so only the negotiation-failure branch of this conditional applies, and broad markets did indeed decline over the course of 2022 consistent with that branch.
With no peace deal reached, Russia did escalate its bombing campaign against Ukrainian cities throughout 2022, and pressure on the US to increase military support grew substantially.
Despite the war continuing and agricultural disruption, the US did not enter a serious recession; the economy achieved a broad soft landing by 2023-2024.
Coordinated sanctions and corporate/CSR-driven economic pressure became a much more prominent and systematic tool in Western foreign policy in the years following the 2022 invasion.
